paper.title_en: Dephasing-Induced Melting of Crystalline Spectral Form Factors
paper.abstract_en: Long-range spectral order can be probed using spectral form factors, where it manifests itself as sharp Bragg peaks at integer multiples of the Heisenberg time in nearly crystalline spectra. We examine how energy dephasing in open systems affects this spectral order and how to control it. We find that Bragg peaks fade algebraically with revival order and dephasing strength, $K_{\rm Bragg}(p)\propto(γp)^{-1/2}$, within an extensive intermediate regime, and persist up to the lifetime of nearest-neighbor coherences despite an extreme decoherence rate. Our results establish the spectral form factor as a probe of spectral order in open quantum systems and identify temporal correlations in spectral fluctuations as a means of controlling it.
